title: The most famous accident in baking probably wasn't an accident

segments.text: The most famous accident in baking probably wasn't an accident.
segments.note: Hook: cookie snapped in half on screen; breaks a belief in under 3 seconds. Viewer wants: then what was it?

segments.text: And the woman behind it wasn't a lucky amateur. She was a trained dietitian.
segments.note: Open loop: who is she? Paid off at t06.

segments.text: The story goes: she ran out of baking chocolate and chopped up a bar instead.
segments.note: Legend (sepia). Viewer waits for the punchline.

segments.text: She expected it to melt. It didn't. Happy accident!
segments.note: Legend payoff, played for fun. Viewer expects the check.

segments.text: Decades later, she brushed that story off. Adding the chocolate, she said, was on purpose.
segments.note: Legend checked, attributed to her. Viewer wants: so who was she?

segments.text: So who was she? Ruth Wakefield. She and her husband ran an inn in Massachusetts.
segments.note: Re-hook at the midpoint; pays off t02. Only person name in the Short.

segments.text: In 1938, her cookie went into her own cookbook, as the Chocolate Crunch Cookie.
segments.note: Journey; only spoken year. Viewer learns the recipe was written down, not stumbled on.

segments.text: A year later, a chocolate company asked to print her recipe on its bars.
segments.note: Journey: the cookie spreads. Viewer wonders what's left to reveal.

segments.text: But here's the twist: chocolate chips didn't exist yet.
segments.note: Twist: the cookie isn't today's cookie yet.

segments.text: Her recipe said to chop the bar into pieces the size of a pea.
segments.note: Process shot: knife on a chocolate bar. Viewer sees how hard it was.

segments.text: That's a lot of chopping. So the company started making chocolate in tiny pieces.
segments.note: Process: bar becomes chips. Viewer connects cookie to chip.

segments.text: The cookie didn't come from the chip. The chip came from the cookie.
segments.note: Twist landed; the trace on today's plate.

segments.text: Crisp edges, a soft middle, and chocolate pieces that hold their shape.
segments.note: Sensation: cookie out of the oven, pieces still whole.
Close: answers the central question, loops to t01, then stop.
